basis.governing_question: How can Metalúrgica Norte cut conversion cost at its Braga plant and put the improvements in place?

sub_questions.question: What is conversion cost per part at the Braga plant today, and where does it build up?
Which improvements can lower conversion cost per part by a measurable amount, and how much is each worth?
How are the chosen improvements put in place at the plant, and in what order?
Do the improvements keep running at the plant, and does cost per part fall against the baseline?

work.unit: Plant conversion cost baseline per part from cost data
Production line observed on the floor with loss analysis

phase_work.why: Baseline first, then three lines observed two at a time; the second round puts the top one week above the archetype's 3 to 6.

work.unit: Improvement put in place on the lines and brought to go-live
Running period after last go-live for cost data to show the effect

phase_work.why: Four improvements put in place two at a time on the three lines, then a running period so cost data can show the effect.

sizing.levers: Carry only the largest sized improvements into Implementation and run more at once; the running period after the last go-live is the floor.

phases.name: Diagnostic
phases.objective_one_line: Establish conversion cost per part at the Braga plant and size the improvements that could lower it.

gate.label: Initiatives go/no-go
gate.decision: Which sized initiatives go into implementation at the plant, and which stop here?

phases.name: Implementation
phases.objective_one_line: Put the agreed improvements in place at the plant and show their effect on conversion cost per part.

gate.label: Final readout
gate.decision: Approve the results against the baseline and the handover to the plant team?

architect_notes: Engagement length is not given; the 15 to 19 weeks are an estimate to confirm before this plan becomes a quote.
Implementation assumes at least 5 weeks of cost data after the last go-live, so any change in cost per part can be measured.
Implementation takes the middle of its 9 to 13 week estimate; slower go-lives or a late cost-data close would push it to 13.
Four improvements carried into Implementation is assumed; every two more or fewer move that phase by 2 to 3 weeks. Confirm after the Diagnostic.
Three production lines come from public research and need the client's confirmation; they set the Diagnostic length.
No Measurement phase: tracking against the baseline stays inside Implementation; confirm whether the client wants tracking after the engagement ends.
